# Generated Files

{/* The markers are spelled out via JS expressions, so that this page is not
    itself taken for a generated file by tools scanning the source. */}

Code generators (Thrift, Protocol Buffers, parser generators, custom scripts)
often produce Erlang modules and header files that nobody edits by hand.
Diagnostics and quick fixes on such files are mostly noise: the fix belongs in
the generator or its input, and any manual edit is lost the next time the file
is regenerated.

ELP recognises two markers that tell it a file is generated:

| Marker | Meaning |
| ------ | ------- |
| <code>{'@'}generated</code> | The whole file is generated. |
| <code>{'@'}partially-generated</code> | The file mixes generated code with hand-written _manual sections_. |

ELP only looks for the markers in the first 2000 bytes of a file, so put them in
the header comment. If a file contains both, it is treated as fully generated.

## Fully generated files

Add the <code>{'@'}generated</code> marker to a comment at the top of the file,
ideally together with a note on how to regenerate it:

<CodeBlock language="erlang">{`%% ${'@'}generated by my_codegen from priv/user.schema. Do not edit by hand.
-module(user_schema).
-export([fields/0]).

fields() ->
    [id, name, email].
`}</CodeBlock>

For a fully generated file:

- Built-in linters skip the file by default. This default can be overridden:
  - by the linter itself, which can opt in to processing generated files, as
    a few do, such as [W0017 - Undefined Function](../../erlang-error-index/w/W0017.md);
  - by the project, which can turn generated files on or off for any linter
    via the [configuration file](#configuring-individual-linters).
- The language server reports compiler diagnostics and the diagnostics of the
  built-in linters that process generated files.
- `elp lint` reports the same diagnostics as the language server, but only
  when the `--include-generated` flag is passed. Without the flag, compiler
  diagnostics and built-in linters skip the file, whatever the linter or the
  configuration file says.
- [`elp search`](../../structural-search.md) skips the file, unless the
  `--include-generated` flag is passed.
- [eqWAlizer](./elp-toml.md#eqwalizer) type-checks the module like any other.

## Partially generated files

Some generators produce a skeleton that is completed by hand, and preserve the
hand-written parts when the file is regenerated. Add the
<code>{'@'}partially-generated</code> marker to the header comment and wrap each
hand-written region between a `% BEGIN MANUAL SECTION` line and a
`% END MANUAL SECTION` line. Anything following `BEGIN MANUAL SECTION` on the
same line is ignored, so it can be used to name the section. Any number of `%`
characters can start the marker lines.

<CodeBlock language="erlang">{`%% ${'@'}partially-generated by my_codegen from priv/user_handler.spec.
%% Only edit the code between the manual section markers.
-module(user_handler).
-export([handle/1]).

handle(Request) ->
    case validate(Request) of
        ok -> process(Request);
        Error -> Error
    end.

validate(#{id := Id}) when is_integer(Id) -> ok;
validate(_Request) -> {error, invalid_request}.

%% BEGIN MANUAL SECTION process
process(#{id := Id}) ->
    {ok, Id}.
%% END MANUAL SECTION
`}</CodeBlock>

For a partially generated file:

- All enabled linters run, including the ones that skip fully generated files.
- Diagnostics inside manual sections are reported as usual, together with their
  quick fixes.
- Diagnostics outside manual sections are dropped by `elp lint`. With the
  `--include-generated` flag, and always in the language server, they are
  reported without quick fixes.

Every `BEGIN MANUAL SECTION` line needs a matching `END MANUAL SECTION` line:
an unterminated section is treated as generated code.

## Configuring individual linters

Whether a linter processes fully generated files can be overridden per linter
via the `include_generated` key in the
[`.elp_lint.toml`](./elp-lint-toml.md#linters) configuration file. The key takes
precedence over the linter's own default, in both directions:

```toml
# Report calls to `erlang:garbage_collect/0` in generated files as well
[linters.no_garbage_collect]
include_generated = true

# Stop reporting undefined functions in generated files
[linters.W0017]
include_generated = false
```

`elp lint` still requires the `--include-generated` flag to process fully
generated files.
